purpose: Test whether the canonical circuit partition P consisting of the supplied Hamiltonian cycle plus the complementary 2-factor can be compressed to its touch-graph / fixed-transversal transition-matroid data and still decide 3-colourability. Give an explicit pair of 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs whose P-touch-graphs, and therefore P-transverse cographic matroids, are identical while their 3-colourability verdicts differ.

common_setup.partition: P={H,F}, where H is the displayed Hamiltonian C7 and F is the complementary C7.
common_setup.touch_graph: Tch(P) has one vertex h for H and one vertex f for F. Every original graph vertex lies on both H and F and therefore becomes one edge h--f. Hence Tch(P) is the two-vertex multigraph with seven parallel edges, independently of the cyclic order of F through the seven original vertices.

exact_checks: In both instances H and F are edge-disjoint 7-cycles, so G=H union F is a simple 4-regular Hamiltonian graph on seven vertices.
Both circuit partitions P have exactly the same labelled touch-graph type: two partition-circuit vertices joined by seven parallel edges corresponding to original graph vertices 0,...,6.
Exhaustive evaluation of all 3^7 colour assignments gives exactly 12 proper colourings for the positive graph and zero for the negative graph.

matroid_statement.source_fact: For a circuit partition P of a 4-regular graph, the transverse matroid determined by the transition set tau(P) is the cographic matroid M*(Tch(P)); modified interlacement matrices represent the same cycle/cocycle information up to the standard identifications.
matroid_statement.consequence: The two instances have isomorphic fixed-P transverse matroids, the same rank/nullity data and the same touch-graph cycle/cocycle structure, yet opposite 3-colourability verdicts.
matroid_statement.scope: This does NOT show that the full transition matroid of the two 4-regular graphs is isomorphic. It rules out only algorithms or certificates whose entire input from the canonical partition P factors through Tch(P), M*(Tch(P)), or equivalent fixed-P cycle-space/nullity data.

lost_information.description: The touch-graph remembers which partition circuits meet at each original vertex, but in the present two-circuit partition every vertex has the same incidence type. It forgets the cyclic permutation/order in which the seven common vertices occur along H versus F.
lost_information.finite_witness: The two explicit F orders differ, and that difference alone is sufficient to change 3-colourability while all fixed-P touch-graph data remains unchanged.
lost_information.frontier: Any surviving circuit-partition route must therefore retain genuine order/interlacement information rather than only the touch-graph transverse matroid.

killed: Decide the pure 4-regular Hamiltonian source only from the touch-graph of P={Hamiltonian cycle, complement 2-factor}.
Decide it only from the fixed-P transverse cographic matroid M*(Tch(P)).
Use only rank/nullity/cycle-space invariants of that fixed partition and claim completeness for 3-colourability.
not_killed: The full transition/isotropic matroid of the 4-regular graph.
Interlacement matrices retaining cyclic-order information relative to an Euler system.
A permutation/interlacement invariant built from the order of complement-cycle ports along H.

next_target.name: E8_HAMILTONIAN_COMPLEMENT_INTERLACEMENT_ORDER_CARRIER_V6_8
next_target.directive: Retain exactly the information v6.7 proves necessary: the cyclic order of common vertices on H relative to each complementary cycle. Construct a polynomial-size permutation/interlacement matrix or circle-system carrier and determine whether nowhere-zero GF(3) tension existence has an exact rank/minimax characterization there. Immediately reject any candidate that factors only through the fixed-P touch-graph or its transverse matroid. Mandatory controls are the v6.7 seven-vertex YES/NO pair, K5, and the fixed-complement-cycle NP-hard Hamiltonian source family.

sources: Lorenzo Traldi, The transition matroid of a 4-regular graph: an introduction, European Journal of Combinatorics 50 (2015), 180-207.
Lorenzo Traldi, Circuit partitions and signed interlacement in 4-regular graphs, Contributions to Discrete Mathematics 20(2) (2025), 456-480.
Herbert Fleischner and Gert Sabidussi, 3-colorability of 4-regular hamiltonian graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 42(2) (2003), 125-140.
